Samish

The Samish Indian Nation’s public account places family, house, village and wider tribal relationships within the Salish Sea region. This guide pairs that historical and cultural introduction with selected accounts of water-quality monitoring and nearshore fish surveys. The Nation’s interpretation and program descriptions remain distinct from independently checked legal conclusions or measured restoration outcomes.

Identity and context

The Samish Indian Nation is a contemporary nation with enduring relationships to the northern Salish Sea region.

03

Family and village relationships in a coastal world

The Nation’s cultural account describes family, house group, village and tribe as connected levels of Samish social life. It places Samish language within Straits Salish and explains the importance of relationships beyond one home community. Its account also connects coastal foods and shore environments with continuing identity. Read this as the Nation’s interpretation, alongside the fuller histories still to be reviewed; the directory has not adopted its historical population estimates or adjudicated legal claims.

Read the sources [4] Samish Indian Nation

04

Following public monitoring work at Fidalgo Bay

The Natural Resources Department reports water-quality sampling in Fidalgo Bay and its streams beginning in 2005, and describes subsequent collaboration with Anacortes on stormwater concerns. Its beach-seining section explains surveys intended to understand nearshore fish use and evaluate habitat restoration. These project descriptions show how readers can follow the Nation’s environmental work. The linked reports and raw data require separate inspection before drawing conclusions about improvement or conditions today.

Read the sources [5] Samish Indian Nation Department of Natural Resources

Samish Culture ↗

Selected actual historical and cultural body discusses Coast Salish/Straits Salish context, kin relationships, household and village groupings, and connections with coastal resources. The Nation’s account is attributed; historical population estimates and its interpretation of court proceedings are not adopted as independent findings.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual Samish Culture and Our Relationship With Nature body, reader lines 154–165. Later legal-history discussion was encountered but underlying decisions not inspected or summarized as holdings; linked film, images and ceremonial details not used.

Review recorded: October 28, 2026

Access note: Actual selected public HTML body read through the web reader; no login or paywall encountered. Linked publications, underlying archives, video/audio and photographs were not thereby fully inspected or cleared for reproduction.

Water Quality & Beach Seining Projects ↗

Selected project descriptions explain Fidalgo Bay monitoring, collaboration on stormwater concerns, and nearshore fish surveys used to evaluate habitat work. Lake Campbell and Thomas Creek sections were also read. Goals, monitoring activities and reported start dates are not claims of independently verified ecological improvement.

Inspection: Content reviewed for the stated scope

Scope: Actual project body, reader lines 151–171: Fidalgo Bay water quality, Lake Campbell, Thomas Creek and Fidalgo Bay beach seining. Linked 2005–2018/2015–2019 data-summary reports, raw sampling data, maps and project photographs not inspected.
